# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 28–37/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 6.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 28. High = (6.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 37. All results are read from code. Your `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay out of the whole site. The pages are also built in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty page. The only unknown is which domain you want as your canonical address. I sampled 2 routes (`/` and `/catalogue`), which is every route. No `geo.config.json` exists, so I assumed you want search and AI tools to find this site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every search and AI-search crawler not to read any page. That makes the rest of the work pointless until it's fixed. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 54–63 (fixes GEO-009 and GEO-014, and the blocker cap no longer applies) ### 2. Put the page content in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** `index.html` ships an empty `
`, and the catalogue list is fetched in the browser. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see nothing. Prerendering or static generation would fix it. - **Where:** `index.html:8`, `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs').then((r) => r.json()).then(setItems);` - **Size:** Large - **Score after this:** 37–46 ### 3. Give each page its own title, description and language - **Why it matters:** Every page currently has the generic title "Vite App", no description and no `lang`. Machines can't tell what a page is about or what language it's in. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 35–44 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, site-wide block | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks Googlebot and Bingbot on 2 of 2 routes. No `noindex` found. | | GEO-015 | Canonical URL | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical tag, and no domain declared to build one | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8`, 2 of 2 routes | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD in the project | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | Not run | No sitemap file, and no `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `index.html:2`, `index.html:5`, 2 of 2 routes | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11`, `/catalogue` is reached only by a button. 1 of 2 routes is clear. | | GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found in the code. There is no middleware or header config. | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`. I read `Home`, `Catalogue` and `Nav`. 1 of 2 routes is clear. | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | Not run | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Optional, not scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored. | ## Other problems found - **Catalogue is reachable only through a button:** `src/main.jsx:11`: ``. Replace it with `Catalogue` so crawlers can follow it. This is also the GEO-016 Problem. - **Image has no alt text:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: ``. Add a description in `alt`. ## Worth considering - **Give each mug its own page:** `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`: `{items.map((m) =>

{m.name}

)}`. Each mug is only a line of text. A page and address per mug would let people and machines land on one mug directly. - **Say more on the home page:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` Buyers will likely want to know prices, sizes and shipping details. Adding that as text might help. - **Label the business with structured data:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol`. Organization or Product JSON-LD could carry facts the page already states, once you have real prices and details. - **Add the viewport tag:** `index.html:4`: ``. A `viewport` meta tag is missing next to it. - **Add a link from Home to the catalogue in the page body:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:4`: `

Handmade ceramic mugs

`. The page that introduces the mugs doesn't link onward to them. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** I don't know which domain is your main address. Tell me the domain and I'll treat the canonical as checkable. - **GEO-011 and GEO-014 (live status codes):** These are live-only checks. They need a running site to confirm that `/api/mugs`, the sitemap URLs and the page responses answer 200. - **Headers set at your host or CDN:** `X-Robots-Tag` and snippet headers could be added outside this repository (GEO-017). - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site. If the `Disallow: /` is deliberate, such as for a staging site, ignore item 1. - Both routes are indexable pages, and you have no sitemap submitted only through a search console. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
